rounds.text: Shankesh Jewellers Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 12.2x [E1], which is exceptionally low compared to the sector benchmark P/E of 24.63x [E6]. The business demonstrates world-class profitability, delivering a 3-year median return on equity of 55% [E18] that spikes to 68.8% for the latest period [E13], completely obliterating the sector benchmark ROE of 8.71% [E9]. Growth metrics are equally impressive, featuring compounded sales growth of 22% over three years [E14] alongside a staggering 165% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E17]. Operational efficiency is steadily improving, with the yearly operating-margin trend moving consistently upward over the last four years [E21] to reach 10% in Mar 2026, up eight percentage points from three years prior [E20]. Furthermore, the company has aggressively strengthened its balance sheet by slashing borrowings down to Rs 66 Cr in Sep 2026 from Rs 168 Cr a year earlier [E27], resulting in a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.12x [E26] and completion of capital expenditure with CWIP dropping to zero [E28]. Investors should be wary of this discrepancy, as it suggests potential issues with receivables or accruals that mask the company's true liquidity [E23]. Furthermore, the stock is currently underperforming, trading below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E38], and it offers a dividend yield of 0.00%, providing no income return to shareholders despite the reported profitability [E4, E46].
